newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian state sets up infrastructure company.
newsitem.headline: Indian state sets up infrastructure company.

text.p: India's western desert state of Rajasthan on Tuesday announced plans to set up an infrastructure development company to help smooth the way for potential investors in the state's large projects.

An official statement said that the firm, the Project Development Corporation (PDCOR), will do the spadework for infrastructure projects in terms of preparing feasibility reports and securing approvals from financial institutions.

PDCOR will develop investment banking reports for mega infrastructure projects like a proposed 15 billion rupees ($419 million) industrial model township, a ten-billion-rupee leisure city, a 10-billion-rupee dry ports project, the statement said.

The firm, a joint venture with the Housing and Development Finance Corp (HDFC) and Infrastructure Leasing and Financial Services (IL&FS), will have a total authorised capital of 50 million rupees, with an initial paid-up capital of 10 million rupees, it added.
Rajasthan state will hold a 24 percent stake in the firm, with IL&FS taking 40 percent and HDFC taking up 36 percent.
The corporation will also tie up for finance with multilateral and bilateral financial institutions when required and offer these projects for implementation to Indian and foreign investors.
